A_general.open_code_note: Bright Data identifies its public brightdata-mcp repository as source code for deploying an instance. The hosted endpoint is managed; the repository is the local/self-hosted variant of the same product. The repository archive was not downloaded in the prepared evidence bundle, so its implementation files were not inspected.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.brightdata.com/sse — official hosted Server-Sent Events endpoint; docs describe the same 32-tool product.
Local/self-hosted Bright Data MCP server — official docs describe a user-operated instance of the product.
https://docs.brightdata.com/general/docs-mcp — separate documentation-search MCP, not the product server.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Bright Data advertises 5,000 free requests/credits per month for new accounts. The MCP server uses the account-level free tier shared across the account; additional usage is charged according to the underlying Bright Data products and account plan. Scraper runs are billed per record.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Web Unlocker and SERP API from $1 per 1,000 requests, Scraper APIs from $0.75 per 1,000 records, and Browser API from $5/GB; pricing depends on product and plan.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP usage draws on a shared account credit pool. The free tier is 5,000 monthly credits/requests. Team account credits are shared across users. Scraper API runs incur per-record billing; discovered records have a documented default limit of 10 per input.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires a Bright Data account and API token or OAuth authorization. Hosted URL parameters can select tool groups/tools and custom unlocker/browser zones. The free tier is account-level; extra credits require a paid plan or contact with an account manager.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official hosted documentation lists 32 tools across search/scraping, scraper APIs, dataset search, browser automation and GEO. It says all are enabled by default, with hosted `groups` and `tools` URL parameters to limit the available set. The local variant has corresponding GROUPS/TOOLS settings.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool-specific outputs include search results, Markdown/HTML page content, structured JSON, scraper run status/results, dataset hits, and browser text/HTML/screenshots/network data. Exact MCP result envelopes and error formats are NOT FOUND.

No product MCP prompt capability is documented in the reviewed materials.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: OAuth 2.1 and MCP authorization support described by vendor
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The provided endpoint responds HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.brightdata.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", scope="mcp"`. Both supplied protected-resource metadata URLs return resource `https://mcp.brightdata.com/mcp`, authorization server `https://brightdata.com`, supported scope `mcp`, and bearer header transport. Supplied authorization-server metadata advertises authorization code and refresh-token grants, S256 PKCE, dynamic registration, resource parameter support, and token endpoint authentication methods `none`, `client_secret_basic`, and `client_secret_post`. It lists scopes `mcp`, `brightdata`, and `offline_access`. Docs also describe API-key authentication by query parameter.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth metadata is JSON. Supplied protected-resource documents list `resource`, `authorization_servers`, `scopes_supported`, and `bearer_methods_supported`. Authorization-server metadata lists issuer and authorization/token/registration/JWKS/introspection endpoints, grants, PKCE, auth methods, scopes and agent-auth metadata. Token lifetime is NOT FOUND.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration; API key. Provided metadata: protected resource scopes_supported=["mcp"], bearer_methods_supported=["header"]; authorization server scopes_supported=["mcp","brightdata","offline_access"], grant_types_supported=["authorization_code","refresh_token"], code_challenge_methods_supported=["S256"], resource_parameter_supported=true, registration_endpoint=`https://brightdata.com/users/auth/mcp/register`, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["none","client_secret_basic","client_secret_post"]. Docs state S256 and resource are mandatory and describe public clients and API token via `?token=`. Token lifetime and revocation behavior NOT FOUND.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official docs distinguish read-style search/scrape/retrieval from scraper execution and browser interaction, but publish no tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint or openWorldHint. 2. No server-enforced confirmation or approval flow is documented; tool guidance recommends sequencing, such as retrieving scraper details before running a scraper. 3. OAuth resource scope is `mcp`; the authorization server metadata advertises `mcp`, `brightdata`, and `offline_access`. Docs describe API-key access and OAuth. Product-role inheritance, admin switches, redirect-URI review and token lifetime/revocation are NOT FOUND. 4. Hosted `groups` and `tools` parameters select tool availability; default is all official tools. Custom unlocker/browser zones are supported. A separate hosted SSE endpoint and local variant are documented. No read-only mode is documented. 5. The server provides access to public web content and datasets. MCP-specific PII masking, output redaction and field boundaries are NOT FOUND. 6. Documented caps: search/scrape batch tools up to 10 requests; dataset search returns up to 10 records per call; scraper run waits up to 45 seconds then may return a snapshot ID; discover methods default to up to 10 records per input; scraper runs are billed per record. 7. MCP schemas are not published in the official reference reviewed. Documentation describes filter tree nesting depth up to three and examples, but detailed validation/correction behavior is NOT FOUND. 8. `session_stats` returns per-tool call counts for the current session. Other audit logging and telemetry behavior are NOT FOUND. 9. No feedback/rating/survey/report tool appears in the official 32-tool list. Third-party Glama listing describes `ask_brightdata_assistant`, which directs questions to vendor support; this name is absent from the official tool reference. Marketing links for the startup program appear on official docs pages. 10. External agent skills are published in the Bright Data skills repository. Official docs include workflow guidance, including the instruction to call `get_scraper_details` before `run_scraper`; whether enforced by server is NOT FOUND. 11. `session_stats` is documented as current-session state. Cross-session memory or behavioral adaptation is NOT FOUND. 12. Hosted `/mcp`, hosted `/sse`, and local/self-hosted variants exist. Docs-search MCP is a separate docs service. 13. No raw arbitrary API request, SQL, script execution or general-purpose escape-hatch tool appears in the official list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Call before `search_dataset` to learn which fields you can filter on.
If `run_scraper` returns status `running` after 45 seconds, call `get_scraper_progress` until the run is ready, then call `get_scraper_results`.
If a run fails, `scrape_as_markdown` works on the same URL as a fallback.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The hosted product exposes a configurable flat tool list. The same vendor also documents an SSE endpoint and local/self-hosted variant, but the reviewed evidence does not show hierarchical or dynamically loaded sub-servers.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference at https://docs.brightdata.com/products/mcp-server/tools.md lists 32 tools and states all are enabled by default. A third-party Glama listing exposes an additional `ask_brightdata_assistant` name and schema; it is included after the official names as third-party evidence and is marked unknown for default enablement. This produces 33 names in actions.json, while the documented official total remains 32. Other catalogue pages reviewed included AgentAtlas and MCPyet; their extracted pages did not establish additional exact native tool names. No proxy-only helper tools were added.

E_aggregated.token_method: Official tool descriptions are available, but verbatim tool schemas and initialize instructions are not. Public repository commit is identified but its implementation files were not available in the prepared local copy, so the specified JSON-character estimate could not be computed.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Bright Data account management and zone configuration are available through the product dashboard, but no account-management tools appear in the MCP list. The FAQ describes creating/configuring zones and changing country targeting in the control panel; MCP accepts a custom zone name but does not document a dedicated country parameter. Sources: https://brightdata.com/pricing/mcp-server ; https://docs.brightdata.com/products/mcp-server/remote/advanced.md

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs recommend workflows including `Call before run_scraper` and advise calling `list_dataset_fields` before `search_dataset`. The docs do not say these sequences are enforced server-side. A 45-second wait and follow-up progress/results calls are described for long scraper runs.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Bright Data's privacy policy says it uses security measures and procedures to reduce misuse and leakage risks, while stating it cannot guarantee absolute system safety. It describes retention as necessary to provide service, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes and enforce policies. The reviewed policy does not specify MCP-specific retention, model-training use, or MCP request logging.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Official pages advertise real-time access to public web data, automatic proxy rotation and handling of bot challenges/CAPTCHAs, a hosted managed server, and 5,000 free monthly requests for new accounts.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented scraping behavior and account credits are product-level claims; the reviewed evidence does not include deployed server code to verify their internal enforcement. Tool filtering and billing limits are documented as configurable/product behavior. Privacy and security statements are general vendor-policy statements rather than MCP-specific technical controls.

contradictions: The supplied protected-resource metadata lists only `mcp` in `scopes_supported`, while the authorization-server metadata lists `mcp`, `brightdata`, and `offline_access`. The OAuth guide says, “The only scope is `mcp`.”

The official tool reference states 32 tools and does not list `ask_brightdata_assistant`; the Glama catalogue lists that name and describes it as a support-assistant tool. It is therefore recorded only as third-party evidence in actions.json.

The tool reference says all 32 tools are enabled by default, while URL parameters can restrict available tools/groups; this is a default-versus-configured behavior difference, not a count discrepancy.
observations_for_research: Tool availability can be restricted through hosted URL parameters or local environment variables, which changes the tool set presented to a client.
The tool collection spans web search and extraction, paid scraper execution, browsing interactions, dataset querying, and calls to external LLM services.
The server documents per-record billing for scraper runs alongside a shared account-level monthly free-credit pool.
